0.0.n: 目 after a number marks its position in a sequence; here it introduces the second reason.

0.1.n: Marks 二つ目 as the topic being explained.

0.3.n: Combines with の to describe agriculture from earlier times.

0.4.n: Links 昔 to 農業, describing when that agriculture belonged.

0.5.n: This noun refers to farming as an activity or way of life.

0.6.n: Marks what something has a relationship with in 関係がある.

0.7.n: Pairs with がある to express being related to something.

0.8.n: Marks 関係 as the thing that exists.

0.9.n: ある is the plain form; 関係がある expresses a relationship.

0.10.n: Turns the preceding statement into a noun phrase that can be identified as the second reason.

0.11.n: Politely ends the explanation identifying the second reason.

1.0.n: A country name; here it broadly refers to the people and their way of life.

1.1.n: Makes 日本 the topic of the sentence.

1.2.n: This adjective describes 間, indicating an extended duration.

1.3.n: 長い間 works as a time expression without needing a particle here.

1.5.n: Combines 米, rice, with 作り, growing or making.

1.6.n: In を中心に, it marks what serves as the central focus.

1.7.n: Used figuratively for the main focus of everyday life.

1.8.n: Completes を中心に, showing what life is organized around.

1.9.n: 暮らす in て-form plus きました shows life continuing from the past toward the present, with a polite ending.

2.0.n: Sets the season for prayers for a good harvest.

2.1.n: Marks 春 as the time when the prayers occur.

2.2.n: Highlights spring in contrast with autumn later in the sentence.

2.3.n: Refers to an abundant crop, the hoped-for outcome of farming.

2.4.n: Marks 豊作 as what people pray for with 祈る.

2.5.n: This linking form of 祈る connects the spring activity to the autumn activity without ending the sentence.

2.7.n: Sets the season for giving thanks after the harvest.

2.8.n: Marks 秋 as the time when thanks are given.

2.9.n: Highlights autumn in contrast with spring.

2.10.n: Combines with に to describe the harvest as completed without problems.

2.11.n: Makes 無事 describe how the harvesting went.

2.12.n: Used with できた to describe successfully bringing in the crop.

2.13.n: Past plain form of できる, indicating that harvesting was successfully accomplished.

2.14.n: Turns the successful harvesting into something people can give thanks for.

2.15.n: Marks the reason for gratitude with 感謝する.

2.16.n: Plain form directly describing お祭り; Japanese places descriptions before the noun.

2.17.n: The prefix お adds a familiar, respectful tone to 祭り.

2.18.n: Marks the festivals as what have been held.

2.20.n: Refers to locations across the country, rather than one particular area.

2.21.n: Marks the locations where the festivals take place.

2.22.n: 行う becomes passive 行われる; てきました adds continuation from the past toward now, with a polite ending.

3.0.n: Points back to the harvest-related festival tradition just described.

3.1.n: Refers to customs passed down over generations.

3.2.n: Marks 伝統 as what continues to exist.

3.4.n: Combines with も to emphasize continuation into the present.

3.5.n: In 今も, it emphasizes that something is still true today.

3.6.n: Refers to the local areas where the festivals are maintained.

3.7.n: Links 地域 to the festivals, identifying them as local celebrations.

3.8.n: Combines with 祭り to form the compound 夏祭り.

3.9.n: Here it is the second part of 夏祭り, naming celebrations held in summer.

3.10.n: Lists examples rather than presenting a complete list of festival types.

3.11.n: A compound of 秋 and 祭り, naming celebrations held in autumn.

3.12.n: Identifies the form in which the tradition survives today.

3.13.n: 残る in て-form plus います describes a continuing state, with a polite ending.

0.lit: The second is the fact that there is a connection with agriculture of the past.
0.tip: こと turns 関係がある into a noun phrase: the fact of having a connection.

1.lit: Japan, for a long time, has lived with rice cultivation at the center.
1.tip: を中心に means centered on something, identifying the main focus of life here.

2.lit: Festivals praying for plentiful harvests in spring and thanking for successful harvesting in autumn have been held in various places.
2.tip: The long description before お祭り tells you what people do at these festivals.

3.lit: That tradition, even now, remains as local summer festivals and autumn festivals.
3.tip: として identifies the form something takes: the tradition survives as local festivals.
